summary: The note curator now runs as a true daily cron instead of every ~300s Dreamer tick; note-candidates keeps its existing hourly cadence. Ships with the curator disabled, matching deployed config.
details: design/dreamer-agent-loop/33-note-dreamer-schedule.md §5, issue #102. `AdaptorSchedule` (design 32/`nora.agent.dreamer`) was watermark-bound: `_dream_adaptor_once` checked the schedule inside the watermark branch, so a `uses_watermark = False` adaptor returned before the check ever ran. `NoteCuratorAdaptor` is exactly that shape and is explicitly time-driven, not data-driven — a note's anchor date passes whether or not the room is talking — so it could not be given a cadence.

The runtime now checks the schedule BEFORE the watermark early return: a watermark-free adaptor with an `AdaptorSchedule` entry fires when `now - last_fired_at >= min_interval_seconds`, with no backlog/lag requirement — a true cron. `last_fired_at` is a per-(adaptor, key) dict in `dream_loop`, the same function-scoped shape as the loop's existing `failures`/`last_failure_at`. A watermark-free adaptor with no schedule entry keeps the pre-existing every-tick behaviour, and the watermark-bearing path (`fact-candidates`) is unchanged and regression-tested.

`nora/app/composition.py` wires `"note-curation"` into `dream_schedules` at `min_interval_seconds=86400` (daily), matching the fact tier's own daily cadence — a note arrangement spans days, so a check more often than once a day buys nothing an hourly `note-candidates` tick has not already fed it. This replaces the every-tick-with-empty-`inputs()`-suppression behaviour, removing a SQL round-trip per workspace per tick that ran forever even though the model call was already being skipped.
limitations: Ships with `[notes] curator_enabled = false` (the deployed default); no running config changes behaviour until an operator turns it on.

Phase offset (design 33 §6/M6) between the create path and the curator is not given new explicit same-tick-exclusion logic. Reviewed instead: `anchored_before` compares against the calendar day strictly (`anchor_date < today`), so a freshly created note cannot be retired same-day unless staged with an already-past anchor. `due_for_revisit` CAN select a freshly created note in the same tick (a note anchored within `REVISIT_LEAD_DAYS=3` gets an immediate `revisit_at`), but selection is not retirement: closing a due note still needs post-creation evidence and, for `closed`, a citation to a message this run showed, both of which are effectively unavailable seconds after creation. Merge-group selection carries the same question now that issue #100 (`note-entity-resolution.json`) gave `note_entity` a writer and merge is reachable — `merge_groups` recomputes live off resolved entities each tick with no note-age floor, so a same-tick collision between a freshly created note and an older one is possible in principle, same as for `due_for_revisit` above. The practical hazard stays low behind `[notes] curator_enabled = false` (the deployed default, unaffected by this cadence change); an explicit same-tick exclusion or a deliberate clock offset remains a documented follow-up, not built here.
